title: Neurooncological register study
summary:
Due to their precarious location in the brain, their invasive growth pattern and the resistance to therapy typical of many brain tumor entities, brain tumors, and diffuse gliomas in particular, are still generally incurable diseases despite increasingly longer survival times. Optimizing the quality of life of affected patients - as opposed to survival alone - is therefore a central task of clinical practice. However, in order to optimize this therapeutic goal, a structured assessment of quality of life and the evaluation of influencing factors is first necessary.
As part of this study, a questionnaire on functionality, psychosocial, emotional and physical well-being as well as frequency of epileptic seizures, pain, side effects of the various antitumor therapies, and medical and nursing care will be handed out to all adult patients of the neuro-oncology clinic at Heidelberg University Hospital who are able to give consent. In addition, various parameters that have already been collected are to be automatically merged from the various hospital systems into a database. The analysis of the collected data should therefore enable a better understanding of the quality of life of neuro-oncology patients and reveal potential areas and opportunities for improvement. In addition, the treating physicians can directly view the results of the questionnaire when the patients present at the neuro-oncology outpatient clinic and make appropriate therapy adjustments - the results of which can be analyzed at the patient's next presentation by completing the questionnaire again, both as part of the study and by the treating physicians.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
All adult patients with a confirmed brain tumor who present at the Neurology Clinic of Heidelberg University Hospital and who are capable of providing information are to be informed and, if they give their consent, included.
Exclusion criteria:
Exclusion criteria are patient age under 18 years, lack of capacity to consent and the absence of a confirmed brain tumor. In addition, patients are excluded if they withdraw their consent to participate in the study.
